messages:
Jane (Support): heads-up — getting multiple urgent tickets from a handful of customers about 5xx + auth failures on the hosted API since the 02:00 deploy. Increasing error rate on /v1/generate. Examples attached. 
Marco (Backend): thanks, grabbing logs now. which region?
Jane (Support): mostly us-west-2 and eu-west-1. One customer (AcmeCorp) saw ~30% of requests return 502/504; another (LayeredAI) saw 401 with 'invalid token' after retry.
Priya (SRE): alerting: sentry shows surge in gateway 502s starting at 02:05 UTC. Latency also climbed for affected requests. CPU/gpu utilization looks normal.
Leo (Platform): I flipped the new auth-strict-verify flag during canary at 01:58, targeted 10% traffic then ramp to 50% at 02:00.
Marco (Backend): oh. flag change + new token validation path could explain 401s. I see stack traces with 'kv-store timeout' in auth service. snippet: 
```
Err=kv.GET timeout at 1500ms | auth/validator.go:142 | verifyToken -> fetchTokenMeta
```
Priya (SRE): also seeing downstream 504s from model-proxy service with logs showing long wait for auth validation: 
```
2026-03-15T02:06:11Z model-proxy request_id=xyz waiting for auth-validate (span: 1200ms)
2026-03-15T02:06:12Z model-proxy upstream timeout to inference-host
```
Dan (Eng): customers are hitting short-lived JWT tokens; token introspection path added a redis lookup. That redis cluster is having slow tails right now on the canary path.
Jane (Support): escalations inbound: two large accounts asked for immediate rollback. Can we get a mitigation?
Leo (Platform): immediate option: roll flag back to previous setting (turn off auth-strict-verify). I can do that but want to confirm scope — currently 35% of traffic on the new path.
Marco (Backend): agree — flip the flag back, start draining canary. Also we should throttle retries to reduce load on auth.
Priya (SRE): rollback will drop new verification. We should also whitelist AcmeCorp/LayeredAI to route them off canary first if possible.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout to platform-auth v3.2 started at 2026-03-15T01:58:27Z; current stable: v3.1
Leo (Platform): doing flag rollback now: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/flags/auth-strict-verify -d '{"value":false}'`
Priya (SRE): marking pages: incident/1928765432 created. Running post-rollback checks.
Marco (Backend): after flip, auth service error rate dropped from 18% -> 2% in 3 minutes for canary cohort.
Jane (Support): I just told AcmeCorp support contact rollback in progress, ETA 5-10m. They replied :thumbsup:.
Dan (Eng): root cause seems to be remote redis timeouts under canary load due to a bad connection pool setting in the new verification path. Patch ready: increase pool size + fallback cache TTL.
Marco (Backend): patch looks good. We'll stage to canary again after we confirm redis tail fixed.
Priya (SRE): questions for follow-up: why didn't chaos test catch redis tail under auth path? Also why did the rollout ramp to 35% so quickly? check rollout policy config.
Leo (Platform): I misconfigured the staged rollout policy — target was 10% -> 30% but autoscaler bumped traffic to 35% when we hit a threshold. I own that; will revert policy and add guardrails.
Jane (Support): any billing/break impact? customers worried about token failures causing duplicate charges.
Dan (Eng): billing logs show no duplicate invoice events; payment pipeline unaffected. But we should audit any request retries that might cause downstream billing effects.
Marco (Backend): collecting sample request_ids for affected customers and will hand to support. Format: `req_YYYYMMDD_xxx`.
Jane (Support): thanks — please include repro steps so support can validate after we redeploy.
Marco (Backend): repro steps: 1) use short-lived token issued within 10s of signing 2) hit /v1/generate concurrently x10 with retries 3) observe intermittent 401 + subsequent 502 from model-proxy. I'll paste exact curl later.
Dan (Eng): temp mitigation idea: increase auth call timeout to 2s and return 429 on auth overload to stop cascade. We can do that if rollback isn't immediate.
Priya (SRE): no need now — rollback looks healthy. Still tracking to 0 anomalies.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: flag change applied by Leo (Platform) at 2026-03-15T02:09:11Z; canary rollback complete.
Leo (Platform): documenting follow-ups: - revert rollout policy defaults - add rate cap for token introspection - ensure canary cap enforced in platform controller - add synthetic tests hitting token path during canary
Marco (Backend): will open PR with redis pool fix + fallback cache. PR: https://git.internal/repo/PR/4582 (includes bench results).
Jane (Support): closing loop with customers now. I'll send post-incident note to AcmeCorp & LayeredAI and offer point-of-contact.
Priya (SRE): timeline + action items: collect additional metrics for redis p99, rollout policy audit, change control blameless review. We should schedule 1-hour postmortem in ops-room at 15:00 UTC.
Dan (Eng): noted. I'll join and bring patch plan.
Leo (Platform): I'll update runbook and add explicit guard check to the console for 'canary traffic > configured limit' alerts.
Jane (Support): thanks all. I'll update the thread with customer confirmations once I have them.
Marco (Backend): sample curl for repro (internal only): 
```
for i in {1..10}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORT_TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"input":"test"}' &
done; wait
```
Jane (Support): AcmeCorp confirmed service normal for them now :white_check_mark:. LayeredAI also confirmed API stable.
Priya (SRE): closing alert but keeping monitoring for 2 hours. We'll publish AMS postmortem doc after the 15:00 review.
Dan (Eng): postmortem action owner list: Marco (auth patch), Leo (rollout guardrails), Priya (monitoring), Jane (customer comms).
Jane (Support): thanks team — great response. :heart:
